title: The tomb of Tutankhamun
text: On 4 November 1922, a boy who was bringing water to a team of archaeologists in the Valley of the Kings found a stone step. It was the beginning of the most famous discovery in the history of archaeology.

The British archaeologist Howard Carter had been looking for the tomb of Tutankhamun for years. His sponsor, Lord Carnarvon, had almost decided to stop paying for the search. When Carter finally found the step, he sent a message to Carnarvon and waited for him to arrive.

When they opened the tomb, Carter looked inside with a candle. Carnarvon asked if he could see anything. Carter answered: Yes, wonderful things! Robbers had entered the tomb in ancient times, but they had not taken most of the treasures.

Inside there were more than five thousand objects: chariots, beds, jewelry and statues. The mummy of the young king was inside three coffins, one inside the other. The last one was made of solid gold. On his face there was the famous golden mask, which now is in a museum in Cairo.

A few months later, Lord Carnarvon died of an infection. Newspapers soon invented the curse of the pharaoh. However, most of the people who had entered the tomb lived for many more years. The real magic of the tomb is what it taught us about ancient Egypt.

grammar.title: Grammar: the past perfect
grammar.rule: Use the past perfect (had + past participle) for an action that happened before another action in the past.
rows: They had not taken the treasures.
When we arrived, he had left.
items: Robbers had ___ the tomb in ancient times.
They had not ___ most of the treasures.
When Carnarvon arrived, Carter had ___ the step.
